en: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
It was late; we went home.
It was late we; went home.
It; was late we went home.
A semicolon joins two closely linked main clauses: “It was late” and “we went home”.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
You will need three things: a pen, a ruler and a rubber.
You will need three: things a pen, a ruler and a rubber.
You will: need three things a pen, a ruler and a rubber.
A colon comes after a complete clause to introduce a list.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
“Come here,” said Mum.
“Come here, said Mum.”
Come here,” said Mum.
Inverted commas go around the spoken words only, with a comma before the closing one.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
My uncle (who lives in Wales) is a farmer.
My uncle (who lives in Wales is a farmer).
My uncle who (lives in Wales) is a farmer.
Brackets go around the extra information, which could be taken out.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
The film – which lasted three hours – was amazing.
The film – which lasted three hours was amazing.
The film which – lasted three hours – was amazing.
A pair of dashes goes around the whole extra part of the sentence.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
The children’s toys were everywhere.
The childrens’ toys were everywhere.
The childrens toys were everywhere.
“Children” is already plural, so we add ’s to show the toys belong to them.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
“Where are you going?” asked Tom.
“Where are you going,” asked Tom?
“Where are you going?” asked Tom?
The question mark belongs to the spoken question, inside the inverted commas.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
I have been to Leeds, England; Paris, France; and Rome, Italy.
I have been to Leeds; England, Paris; France, and Rome; Italy.
I have been to Leeds, England, Paris; France and Rome, Italy.
Semicolons separate list items that already contain commas.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
I was soaked: it had poured all day.
I was: soaked it had poured all day.
I was soaked it had: poured all day.
A colon can introduce an explanation of the first clause.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
The dog wagged its tail.
The dog wagged it’s tail.
The dog wagged its’ tail.
“Its” without an apostrophe shows belonging. “It’s” means “it is”.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
We bought eggs, milk, bread and jam.
We bought, eggs milk bread and jam.
We bought eggs milk, bread, and, jam.
Commas separate the items in a list.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
After lunch, we played outside.
After, lunch we played outside.
After lunch we, played outside.
A comma goes after a fronted adverbial like “After lunch”.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
“I’m hungry,” said Ben, “so let’s eat.”
“I’m hungry,” said Ben, so let’s eat.”
“I’m hungry, said Ben, so let’s eat.”
Each part of the spoken words needs its own pair of inverted commas.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
The Nile (the longest river in Africa) flows north.
The Nile (the longest river in Africa flows north).
The (Nile the longest river in Africa) flows north.
Brackets go around the extra information only.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
Sam loves football; his sister prefers tennis.
Sam loves; football his sister prefers tennis.
Sam loves football his; sister prefers tennis.
The semicolon sits between the two linked main clauses.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
There was only one thing to do – run!
There was only – one thing to do run!
There was only one – thing to do run!
A single dash can add a dramatic ending after a complete clause.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
Dad had one rule: no phones at dinner.
Dad had: one rule no phones at dinner.
Dad: had one rule no phones at dinner.
The colon comes after the complete clause and introduces the rule.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
We’re going to the zoo, aren’t we?
Were going to the zoo, arent we?
We’re going to the zoo, are’nt we?
The apostrophe goes where letters are missing: we are → we’re, are not → aren’t.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
Mum said, “Tidy your room.”
Mum said, Tidy your room.”
Mum said “, Tidy your room.”
The spoken words need inverted commas at both ends, with a comma before them.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
The women’s team won the cup.
The womens’ team won the cup.
The womens team won the cup.
“Women” is already plural, so we add ’s to show belonging.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
I ate the cake (all of it).
I ate the cake (all of it.)
I ate (the cake all of it).
The full stop ends the whole sentence, so it goes after the closing bracket.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
Bring the following items: a hat, a coat and some gloves.
Bring the: following items a hat, a coat and some gloves.
Bring the following: items a hat, a coat and some gloves.
The colon comes straight after “items” to introduce the list.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
The sky went dark; a storm was coming.
The sky went dark, a storm was coming.
The sky; went dark a storm was coming.
A comma cannot join two main clauses on its own, but a semicolon can.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
My best friend – a girl called Zara – lives next door.
My best friend – a girl called Zara lives next door.
My best – friend a girl called Zara – lives next door.
The pair of dashes goes around the extra information about the friend.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
Did you remember your bag?
Did you remember your bag.
Did you remember? your bag
A question ends with a question mark.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
“Watch out!” shouted Kim.
“Watch out”! shouted Kim.
“Watch out!” Shouted Kim.
The exclamation mark goes inside the inverted commas, and “shouted” keeps a small letter.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
My brother, who is twelve, loves skateboarding.
My brother, who is twelve loves skateboarding.
My brother who, is twelve, loves skateboarding.
Commas go on both sides of the extra information “who is twelve”.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
There is one thing I hate: getting up early.
There is one: thing I hate getting up early.
There: is one thing I hate getting up early.
The colon comes after the complete clause and reveals what the thing is.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
Lucy’s brother is very tall.
Lucys brother is very tall.
Lucys’ brother is very tall.
For one owner, we add ’s: the brother belongs to Lucy.
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
I love summer; winter is too cold for me.
I love summer; winter, is too cold for me.
I love; summer winter is too cold for me.
The semicolon links two related main clauses, with no extra comma.

example.answer_en: It was late; we went home.
example.why_en: A semicolon joins two closely linked main clauses: “It was late” and “we went home”.

en.title: Punctuation
en.teach: Semicolons join linked clauses; colons introduce lists or explanations: like this. Dashes – and brackets (like these) – add extra information. Inverted commas go around spoken words.
